title: Check yourself: Results, annotations and large tool sets, and the practice

questions.stem: A `search_orders` tool returns every match, sometimes thousands of rows, and fills the context before the agent can act. What change helps most?

options.text: Send all the rows and ask the model to skip the extras
options.says: Ruled out because "Bloated responses waste context and make it harder for Claude to extract what matters."

options.text: Serve one page, a cursor and a note on narrowing
options.says: A page with a cursor bounds the result, and the note tells the agent how to go on.

options.text: Cut the list at a fixed length and add no message
options.says: Ruled out because "If you choose to truncate responses, be sure to steer agents with helpful instructions."

options.text: Move to a larger context window and send the full list
options.says: Ruled out because the article expects "the need for context-efficient tools to remain".

questions.stem: A `find_documents` tool answers with the sentence "Found these documents: Maintenance Schedule, Lab Access Plan." The next tool, `read_document`, requires an exact handle for one document, and the agent keeps making them up. What change fits best?

options.text: Return each hit with a stable identifier and the fields the following step needs
options.says: The tool should hand the next step a real identifier, in a result trimmed to what that step needs.

options.text: Add a prompt rule that tells the model to derive each id from the title it was shown
options.says: Ruled out because the documentation asks the tool to "Return semantic, stable identifiers (for example, slugs or UUIDs) rather than opaque internal references", not the model to reconstruct them.

options.text: Return every stored field of each hit, so that nothing is missing
options.says: Ruled out because a result should "include only the fields Claude needs to reason about its next step".

options.text: Lengthen the sentence, describing each document in more prose
options.says: Ruled out because more prose adds length and no handle: "Bloated responses waste context and make it harder for Claude to extract what matters."
